questions.question: The Mahabharata is traditionally attributed to:
questions.rationale: Ved Vyasa (Krishna Dvaipayana) is the traditional compiler-author; the epic runs to 18 parvas and includes the Bhagavad Gita within the Bhishma Parva.

questions.question: 'Arthashastra', the ancient treatise on statecraft, was written by:
questions.rationale: Kautilya's Arthashastra is the Mauryan-era manual of governance and strategy — the book examiners attach to 'statecraft' every single time.

questions.question: 'India Wins Freedom' was written by:
questions.rationale: Azad's account of the freedom movement and Partition anchors the memoir set along with Nehru's Discovery of India and Gandhi's autobiography.

questions.question: 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of:
questions.rationale: Kalam's Wings of Fire (with Arun Tiwari) traces the missile scientist's path from Rameswaram to the Pokhran era.

questions.question: 'Anandamath', the novel containing the hymn 'Vande Mataram', was written by:
questions.rationale: Bankim Chandra's 1882 novel of sanyasis in famine-struck Bengal gave the national song its text — a fact that doubles as a national-symbols question.

questions.question: The 'Booker of Bookers' was awarded to:
questions.rationale: Salman Rushdie's Midnight's Children won the Booker (1981) and then the 'Booker of Bookers' anniversaries — the best-known fact in Indian English fiction.

questions.question: 'The Wealth of Nations' was written by:
questions.rationale: Adam Smith's 1776 treatise founded modern economics with its division of labour and the invisible hand — the same year as the American Declaration of Independence.

questions.question: 'Rajatarangini', the history of Kashmir, was written by:
questions.rationale: Kalhana's 12th-century chronicle is India's first properly historical narrative — the answer whenever 'history of Kashmir' appears.

questions.question: 'Das Kapital' was written by:
questions.rationale: Marx wrote Das Kapital; Engels co-authored only the Communist Manifesto and later edited Capital's later volumes — the collaboration the question exploits.

questions.question: 'Gitanjali', the work that won the 1913 Nobel Prize, was composed by:
questions.rationale: Tagore's Gitanjali (Song Offerings) made him the first non-European Nobel laureate — the anchor fact of Indian literature in every GK paper.
